official.application_cycle: Academic year 2027-2028 (fellowship runs September to January)
official.status_note: The official NIAS page is labelled 'Application Closed'; the call for the academic year 2027-2028 opens on 15 January 2027 and closes on 15 March 2027, 12.00 noon CET.
official.tuition_coverage_note: NIAS publishes no tuition terms for the KB Fellowship; it is a non-degree research residency rather than a study programme.
benefits: Five months of funded research time at NIAS in Amsterdam, from September to January; one fellowship per academic year
Personal stipend of EUR 3,500 per month, paid directly to the fellow (fellows without an affiliation and fellows from outside the Netherlands)
For scholars affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute, a Dutch University Grant of EUR 3,500 per month paid to the institution instead
An office and research facilities at NIAS, plus full use of the KB's collections, facilities, services and expertise
Subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible (fellow contributes EUR 975 per month), or reimbursement of local public transport
Participation in the academic, community and outreach programme of an international community of scholars, writers and artists
eligibility: Open to scholars, with or without an institutional affiliation, with at least three years of research experience after obtaining their PhD on the closing date of the call
Open to creative practitioners, with or without an affiliation, with at least three years of independent practice since graduating or equivalent experience
The project must relate to the KB research agenda or extend its scope; proposals with an international or comparative perspective are especially welcome
A fellowship is a full-time commitment; fellows must be at the institute four days a week from the start to the end of the semester
Excellent command of spoken and written English; a test or interview may form part of the selection procedure
requirements: Submit the application through the online application form
A project proposal of no more than 1,500 words, including footnotes and excluding references
An academic or artistic CV of no more than four pages, including any international collaborations and a list of key publications
A statement of no more than 300 words explaining how the project relates to the applicant's work so far and why the fellowship comes at the right time
Be available at NIAS four days a week for the whole semester
Be willing to publish any resulting publications under the Creative Commons CC BY 4.0 licence
documents: Project proposal (maximum 1,500 words, footnotes included, references excluded)
Academic or artistic CV (maximum four pages, with international collaborations and key publications)
Statement (maximum 300 words on fit and timing)
selection_criteria: The quality and originality of the proposal
The candidate's scholarly or artistic achievements so far
What the candidate expects from the NIAS community and will contribute to it
The significance of the project for the policies and practices of the KB or of libraries in general, or for the place of the library in a liberal democracy
coverage: Personal stipend of EUR 3,500 per month, paid directly to the fellow
Dutch University Grant of EUR 3,500 per month, paid to the institution, for scholars affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute who continue to receive their salary
Office and research facilities at NIAS
Subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible: the fellow contributes EUR 975 per month and NIAS contributes EUR 1,350 per month; otherwise reimbursement of local public transport

Travel expenses: a return-ticket allowance capped by distance (max EUR 0.25 per km within 500 km in Europe, max EUR 500 within Europe beyond 500 km, max EUR 1,500 from outside Europe) and up to EUR 250 per month commuting reimbursement for Dutch-based fellows
application_method: Wait for the call to open on 15 January 2027 (the page currently shows 'Application Closed')
Complete the online application form on the NIAS website
Upload the project proposal, the CV and the statement
official.application_route: Online application form on the NIAS website during the annual call, 15 January to 15 March 2027
official.study_mode: Full-time residency; attendance at the institute four days a week
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; the fellowship is open in the Netherlands and abroad, with or without institutional affiliation. Personal stipends are granted to fellows without an affiliation and fellows from outside the Netherlands; scholars affiliated with a Dutch university receive a Dutch University Grant paid to their institution.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to researchers and creative practitioners from any country; fellows living outside the Netherlands are eligible for the personal stipend and, where available, subsidised accommodation
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all scholarly and artistic disciplines, but the project must relate to the KB research agenda or extend its scope
official.research_requirement: A project proposal of no more than 1,500 words is required; artists may propose artistic production as a research strategy or research ahead of production, and NIAS does not provide studios, materials or tools
official.description: The KB Fellowship at NIAS offers researchers and creative practitioners five months to work on the future of the (public) library, or on the library as a public institution and a pillar of liberal democracy. NIAS and the KB, the National Library of the Netherlands, established the current fellowship in 2025, continuing an earlier KB Fellowship that ran from 2004 to 2018.
official.program_type: Residential fellowship at a national institute for advanced study, offered by NIAS in partnership with the KB, the National Library of the Netherlands
official.english_requirement: English is the working language at NIAS; applicants should speak and write it well enough to take a full part in the life of the institute and to benefit from the responses of their peers. A test or interview may form part of the selection procedure; no IELTS or TOEFL score is published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a single five-month residential fellowship (September to January) in Amsterdam, one per year, for a researcher or creative practitioner whose project speaks to the future of the public library, funded at EUR 3,500 per month paid directly to the fellow - or the same amount routed through a Dutch employer as a Dutch University Grant. The 2027-2028 round opens 15 January 2027 and shuts at noon CET on 15 March 2027, so the window is roughly two months and the application goes in as one complete package: form, proposal, CV and statement. With only one fellowship annually and a KB-appointed committee ranking eligible applicants against four published criteria, a proposal that merely restates existing work will not survive the cut.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A mid-career scholar or artist at least three years past the PhD or graduation who wants protected time in Amsterdam to work on the library's place in public life and can be on site four days a week.
application_readiness_checklist: Diary the exact timing now: the form opens 15 January 2027 and closes 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET, leaving time in February for a colleague to read the proposal
Check the three-year clock early: research experience after the PhD, or independent creative practice, is measured on the closing date, not the opening date
Draft the 300-word statement around why this specific semester is the right moment - it is a ranked question, not a formality
Map the project explicitly onto the KB research agenda and be ready to say what new questions it brings rather than what it continues

If you are Dutch-affiliated, secure your dean's or department chair's agreement before applying: the Dutch University Grant requires the institution to continue paying your salary and sign the Fellowship Agreement terms
Plan for housing uncertainty before you apply: accommodation is limited and NIAS may ask randomly selected fellows to arrange their own lodging in the city
common_rejection_risks: Proposals that summarize ongoing work instead of opening a new question - the KB ranking committee explicitly prefers proposals that bring new questions or unexpected dimensions to the research agenda
A thin 'why now' statement: 300 words is short, and a generic timing argument wastes one of the four ranked criteria
Breaching the hard word and page limits (1,500 words including footnotes, four-page CV, 300-word statement)
Being unable to commit four days a week on site for the full five months - this is a full-time residency, not a visiting-scholar arrangement
Dutch-affiliated applicants applying without institutional consent, which the Dutch University Grant route depends on
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housed fellows still contribute EUR 975 per month for subsidised accommodation (about EUR 4,875 over the five months). NIAS does not reimburse travel insurance, excess baggage, parking or family members' travel, and anything above the capped travel allowance is out of pocket. On the Dutch University Grant route the EUR 3,500 goes to the institution, not the fellow. A NIAS fellowship is not employment, so pension and social-insurance contributions remain with your own institution or yourself.
document_audit: The 1,500-word proposal limit counts footnotes but excludes references - trim the body text and bibliography separately
The four-page CV is expected to show international collaborations and recent key publications, preferably in refereed journals or books
The 300-word statement has a hard ceiling; cutting to it usually means losing the weakest sentences, not required content
Accepting the award commits any resulting publications to CC BY 4.0 - factor this in if you plan a monograph under traditional copyright terms
Artists get no studio, materials or tools from NIAS, so production ambitions must be framed as a research strategy or research ahead of production
alerts: The official page currently shows 'Application Closed' - the next round only opens on 15 January 2027; earlier submissions are not accepted
Only one KB Fellowship is awarded per academic year, so there is no second chance in the same cycle
The Fellowship Advisory Committee balances the cohort by discipline, location, career stage and gender, so a strong proposal can miss out on portfolio fit
Accommodation is limited: NIAS may ask randomly selected fellows to find housing in the city themselves, with a subsidy of up to EUR 1,350 per month
Fellows from low-income countries may request additional support via the NIAS Solidarity Fund - resources are limited, so raise it early with the Partnership Officer
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online form submitted during the call window; NIAS screens all applications for eligibility first, a KB-appointed ranking committee then scores eligible candidates and returns the ranking to NIAS, where the Fellowship Advisory Committee advises the Director, who makes the final decision.
